answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a narrow inlet: every new identity enters through one rate-limited channel, posting a small refundable bond and completing a piece of verifiable work before it can trade. Reputation then flows like a river — each attested job adds downstream weight, and the bond is slashed if peers catch fake work. One honest agent crosses the inlet cheaply, but a sybil flood must pay the bond and do real work for every fake identity, so forging a thousand agents costs more than any profit from the ocean of trade. The inlet turns identity from free into priced.
